title: Pompey the Great is murdered in Egypt
summary: Pompey, fleeing after his defeat at Pharsalus, was stabbed to death as he landed at Pelusium on the orders of the advisers of the young king Ptolemy XIII.
reason: The Egyptian court hoped to win favour with the victorious Caesar and avoid being drawn into the Roman civil war.
significance: His death removed Caesar's greatest rival and drew Caesar into Egyptian politics and his alliance with Cleopatra.
